current_bottleneck: The support-object bottleneck remains upstream in Stage A, but 286a shows the issue is no longer raw-vs-anchored interpolation. A local history-coordinate transport recovers much more statistical validity while keeping strong change-law realism, yet level KS is still dead and short-horizon active mean reversion still fails. The likely next question is whether the scale part of the affine transport is overshooting the central level law.
last_result_summary: Iteration 106 ran 286a-v0, an evaluation-only history-affine support transport on top of the existing 283a reweighting checkpoint. It scored 4/11, passed surface, block_ar, cointegration, and cross_cell_correlation, recovered much more validity than raw-future support, but still left level KS at 0/25 and did not break the frontier.
next_step_recommendation: Run a small follow-up support-object experiment that isolates the scale component of the new history-coordinate family, starting with a mean-only history transport.
current_best_model: 277d-v0, 279a-v0, 281a-v0, 281b-v0, and 282b-v0 are the current overall co-frontiers at 5/11 in the two-level reset.
current_best_note: 282b is still the cleanest current Stage B objective frontier at 5/11, but 284b and 285a strengthen the conclusion that the real cap is now the Stage A support object rather than the Stage B weighting law.
